| [HugAgent: A Human Simulation Benchmark for Individual-Level Reasoning](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2510.15144>) | EMNLP 2026 Main · Accepted | Benchmarks whether models can recover a person’s beliefs and predict belief updates under intervention, using questionnaires and think-aloud interviews across three policy domains. |
| [Simulating Society Requires Simulating Thought](<https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/abdf9f11e8d8206f5db7dce6b34cd292-Abstract-Position_Paper_Track.html>) | NeurIPS 2025 · Position Track | Proposes RECAP to evaluate reasoning fidelity through causal traceability, demographic grounding, and intervention consistency. |
| [Can Large Language Model Agents Simulate Human Trust Behavior?](<https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/1cb57fcf7ff3f6d37eebae5becc9ea6d-Abstract-Conference.html>) | NeurIPS 2024 | Compares agent decisions in trust games with human trust behavior. |
| [SOTOPIA: Interactive Evaluation for Social Intelligence in Language Agents](<https://openreview.net/forum?id=mM7VurbA4r>) | ICLR 2024 | Introduces interactive social scenarios and a framework for evaluating agents’ social goals. |
| [Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples](<https://doi.org/10.1017/pan.2023.2>) | Political Analysis 2023 | Compares simulated survey answers across demographic groups with human survey responses. |
| [Using Large Language Models to Simulate Multiple Humans and Replicate Human Subject Studies](<https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/aher23a.html>) | ICML 2023 | Introduces Turing Experiments to test replication of classic human-subject findings. |
| [Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?](<https://proceedings.mlr.press/v202/santurkar23a.html>) | ICML 2023 | Compares language-model opinion distributions with public-opinion surveys across 60 demographic groups. |
| [Social Simulacra: Creating Populated Prototypes for Social Computing Systems](<https://doi.org/10.1145/3526113.3545616>) | UIST 2022 | Evaluates whether generated online communities and interactions resemble real community behavior and support design exploration. |
